earliest_visible_sign.description: Minute pale-yellow or chlorotic flecks on leaves that enlarge into small tan spots that become slightly raised

characteristic_sign_or_lesion.description: Circular to oval or slightly elongated powdery pustules that rupture the leaf epidermis and release powdery spores on both upper and lower leaf surfaces

colors.color_progression: pale yellow or chlorotic flecks to tan spots to cinnamon-brown/orange-brown/reddish-brown pustules to dark brown/black pustules

shape.shape_progression: Minute chlorotic flecks enlarge into tan, raised spots, then pustules break through the epidermis

size.size_variation_note: Size and shape can vary between common rust and southern rust and between plant tissues

advanced_or_severe_stage.description: Pustules darken to brown-black as teliospores replace urediniospores, giving a rusty or peppered appearance.
advanced_or_severe_stage.coalescence: Pustules multiply and may occur in scattered patches or bands.
advanced_or_severe_stage.tissue_death_appearance: severe infections cause yellowing, premature drying, and death of leaves or leaf sheaths

distribution_on_plant.vertical_pattern: Pustules can form in bands when infection occurs while leaves are emerging from the whorl
distribution_on_plant.horizontal_pattern: Scattered patches or bands; most conspicuous on leaves and often visible on both leaf surfaces.
distribution_on_plant.other_parts_if_severe: may extend to leaf sheaths, husks, tassels, and stalks

pathognomonic_features: Cinnamon-brown, orange-brown, or reddish-brown circular to oval powdery pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces that eventually turn dark brown to black.
